title: The tower Stalin gave Warsaw
episode: Palace of Culture and Science: Stalins hated Gift to Poland
description: Megaprojects, an engineering history channel, on the Palace of Culture and Science, Stalin’s ‘gift’ built by Soviet workers in 1952–55. At 237 metres with its spire it was long Poland’s tallest building, and many Varsovians still resent it.

title: Old shop signs saved from the scrapheap
episode: Warsaw Neon Museum – where old signs tell powerful stories | David Hill
description: TVP World, Poland’s English-language public broadcaster, talks to David Hill, co-founder of the Neon Muzeum, which rescues cold-war neon signs from Warsaw’s shops and cafés. It fills a former factory hall in the Soho Factory complex in Praga.

title: The last king’s bathhouse palace
episode: Is Warsaw’s Royal Łazienki Europe’s Most Beautiful Park? | Pulse of Culture
place: Palace on the Isle, Łazienki Park
description: TVP World’s ‘Pulse of Culture’ tours Royal Łazienki, the park of Poland’s last king, Stanisław August Poniatowski. Łazienki means ‘baths’: its Palace on the Isle began as a bathhouse that he turned into a summer palace in the 1780s.

title: Socialist realism on Constitution Square
episode: MDM: Socialist Realism Urban Planning | GOOD IDEA
description: Radosław Gajda explains MDM, the Marszałkowska Residential District built in 1950–52 in socialist realism, the Soviet-imposed official style. Its showpiece, Constitution Square, has arcades, giant lamp standards and reliefs of model workers.

title: The 1920 battle Poles call a miracle
episode: The Battle of Warsaw and Lenin's "enormous defeat"
description: The History Guy, an American history channel, on the Battle of Warsaw in August 1920, when Polish forces stopped the Red Army near the capital: the ‘Miracle on the Vistula’. Józef Piłsudski, Poland’s head of state, then lived in Belweder Palace.

title: A café where Warsaw’s poets held court
episode: To the cafe "Mała Ziemiańska" - online tours | POLIN Museum
place: Site of Mała Ziemiańska café, Mazowiecka Street
description: POLIN, the museum of Polish Jewish history, visits the site of Mała Ziemiańska, the interwar café on Mazowiecka Street where poets such as Julian Tuwim and Antoni Słonimski held court. It was destroyed in 1944.

title: The ghetto, told by the museum that will house its story
place: Warsaw Ghetto Museum, former Bersohn and Bauman Children’s Hospital
description: The Warsaw Ghetto Museum’s account of the ghetto, sealed in November 1940, where some 400,000 Jews were confined. The museum is moving into the Bersohn and Bauman Children’s Hospital on Sienna Street, one of the few ghetto buildings left.
